input.brief: Should we expand into the European market? We have four hundred pro customers and want to reach eight hundred.

candidates.label: served_v17
candidates.note: Verbatim decision_review object extracted from the arm's raw model text (json_text).

output.narrative_summary: This result rests on the link from Competitive Intensity to Revenue Growth. If competition intensifies beyond current levels, more runs could support a different option. In this model, 72% of runs supported Enter European Market.

story_headlines.opt_expand: Enter European Market benefits from a modelled link between market entry and revenue growth that holds under most variations.
story_headlines.opt_wait: Delay to Next Year would need competitive intensity to rise substantially for more runs to support it instead.

robustness_explanation.summary: The ordering holds in about 91% of variations, based on current estimates.
robustness_explanation.primary_risk: The link from Competitive Intensity to Revenue Growth is the main source of fragility in this result.
stability_factors: The link from Europe Market Entry to Revenue Growth anchors this result strongly.
Pricing Power contributes a steady, positive relationship to Revenue Growth.
fragility_factors: The link from Competitive Intensity to Revenue Growth could shift the comparison if competition intensifies.

output.readiness_rationale: The comparison is settled on your numbers: Europe Market Entry anchors the result strongly, with only the Competitive Intensity relationship left as a watch item.

fac_competition.specific_action: Commission a short competitor scan of pricing and share moves in the target European market segments.
fac_competition.rationale: Competitive Intensity is the main relationship that could shift this comparison.
fac_competition.decision_hygiene: Estimate the likely competitive intensity before reviewing the scan results.

edge_competition_revenue.trigger_description: If Competitive Intensity rises substantially relative to Revenue Growth expectations...
edge_competition_revenue.consequence: ...then the most runs would support Delay to Next Year rather than Enter European Market.

flip_thresholds.narrative: If Competitive Intensity moves from 35% to 62%, more runs would support a different option.

key_assumptions: The link from Competitive Intensity to Revenue Growth assumes current competitive conditions in Europe hold.
The link from Pricing Power to Revenue Growth assumes pricing power can be maintained through expansion.
Growing from four hundred to eight hundred pro customers is taken as the measure of successful expansion.

decision_quality_prompts.question: What would make you switch to Delay to Next Year?
decision_quality_prompts.applies_because: Enter European Market holds a strong share of modelled runs, so it is worth naming what would change that conclusion.

decision_quality_prompts.question: This failed because Competitive Intensity rose faster than expected, what signs would show that early?
decision_quality_prompts.applies_because: The comparison is settled enough to act on, but the Competitive Intensity relationship is the one open watch item.

pre_mortem.failure_scenario: Expansion failed because Competitive Intensity rose sharply, weakening the link from Competitive Intensity to Revenue Growth faster than pricing power could offset it.
warning_signs: New entrants or price cuts appearing in target European segments
Pricing Power showing early signs of erosion in customer conversations
pre_mortem.mitigation: Commission a competitor scan before committing full expansion resources.
pre_mortem.review_trigger: Reconvene if competitive intensity signals emerge before launch.
